Tere Ride Sharing Nigeria is a modern, user-friendly ride-sharing web application designed to connect passengers with nearby drivers in real time. The platform focuses on seamless booking, efficient route matching, and a smooth user experience for both riders and drivers.

projects.longDescription:
Tere Ride Sharing Nigeria – Full-Stack Ride Sharing Platform (Completed Project)

Tere Ride Sharing Nigeria is a modern web-based ride-sharing platform designed to streamline urban transportation by efficiently connecting passengers with available drivers in real time. The system is built with a focus on speed, reliability, and ease of use, ensuring a smooth experience for both riders and drivers across busy Nigerian cities.

The platform allows users to quickly register, log in, and book rides based on their current location and destination. Riders can view available drivers nearby, estimate fares, and confirm bookings within seconds. On the driver side, the system provides a simple interface to accept ride requests, navigate routes, and manage trip status from pickup to drop-off.

A key strength of this project is its clean and responsive user interface, optimized for both desktop and mobile devices. The design prioritizes usability, ensuring that even first-time users can easily understand and interact with the platform without confusion. Real-time interaction flows simulate the core logic of modern ride-hailing applications, making the experience intuitive and efficient.

From a technical perspective, the project demonstrates strong understanding of full-stack development principles, including frontend UI design, backend logic handling, and data flow management between users and drivers. The architecture is designed to be scalable, allowing future enhancements such as live GPS tracking, dynamic pricing, in-app payments, and rating systems.

Security and performance considerations have also been taken into account, ensuring safe authentication processes and optimized request handling for fast response times. The system structure is modular, making it easier to maintain, debug, and extend with additional features.

Overall, Tere Ride Sharing Nigeria reflects a real-world transportation solution concept, showcasing the ability to design and develop a production-style application that solves practical mobility challenges in a growing urban environment.

projects.title: ZEX Rates Aggrigator
projects.description:
ZEX Rates is a courier rate management platform for freight agents and clients. Admins upload Excel rate sheets from multiple carriers (Aramex, DHL, UPS, APX, etc.) — the system auto-detects and parses 17+ proprietary formats into a
  unified database. Users search by destination, service, and weight to get instant price comparisons with automatic markup applied. Clients see anonymized options; agents and admins see real provider names. Built with FastAPI, React, and
   React Native, backed by Supabase, and deployed across HuggingFace Spaces, Vercel, and Expo.
projects.longDescription:
● ZEX Rates — Full Project Description

  Overview
  ZEX Rates is a full-stack, multi-platform courier rate management and quote comparison system built for ZEX International, a freight and logistics company. The platform solves a real operational problem: courier providers each supply
  rate sheets in their own proprietary Excel formats, making it impossible to compare prices across carriers without manual work. ZEX Rates eliminates that entirely — admins upload raw carrier spreadsheets, the system parses and  normalizes them, and clients get instant price comparisons across all active carriers in seconds.

  ---
  The Problem It Solves

  Freight agents traditionally receive rate cards from each courier as Excel files, all structured differently. To quote a shipment, an agent would open multiple spreadsheets, manually look up the destination country, find the right
  weight bracket, apply a markup, and repeat for every carrier. With dozens of countries, multiple weight tiers, zone-based pricing logic, and different markup rules per client, this process was error-prone and time-consuming.

  ZEX Rates automates the entire pipeline — from raw Excel upload to instant quote delivery — across web and mobile.

  ---
  Complexity

  This project is significantly more complex than a typical CRUD application. The difficulty comes from three areas in particular.

  1. The File Parsing Engine

  The single hardest technical challenge was building an Excel parser that could handle 17+ distinct carrier file formats — each with its own column layout, sheet structure, naming conventions, and pricing logic. Carriers like Aramex
  structure rates as a flat grid where each row is a country and columns represent weight tiers. DHL and UPS use a two-sheet zone system: one sheet maps countries to zones, another maps zones to prices. APX has several sub-variants
  depending on origin hub (Dubai, Australia, Amsterdam). Some files are transposed, some use merged cells, some embed pricing in non-standard rows.

  Rather than writing fragile format-specific parsers in isolation, we built a type detection system that inspects column headers, sheet names, and data patterns to identify the file type before parsing begins. Once detected, the
  appropriate parser runs and normalizes all data into a single schema: (country, country_code, weight_kg, price, zone, rate_type). This makes every carrier's rates queryable in exactly the same way regardless of source format.

  Special-case handling was required for:
  - Australia: 4,813 postcodes mapped to carrier zones, stored as a lookup in the settings table
  - Canada: Postal prefix → zone resolution
  - Zone-based carriers: A two-step resolution — country → zone → rate lookup
  - Per-kg extension pricing: Some carriers charge a base rate up to a threshold then per-kg above it

  2. The Rate Calculation Engine

  Once rates are parsed, the calculation engine handles quote requests. Given a destination country, service type, and weight, it must:
  - Find all active carrier files assigned to that country and service
  - Determine the correct pricing strategy for each file (direct, zone-based, or single-destination)
  - Resolve the correct weight bracket or zone
  - Apply the global markup percentage set by the admin
  - Return results sorted by final price

  The strategy is inferred from the file_type field stored at upload time, not from the data shape at query time — a deliberate architectural decision to avoid fragile runtime inference.

  3. Multi-Role, Multi-Platform Access

  The platform serves three distinct user roles (admin, agent, client) across four surfaces (admin web, client web, Android mobile, and the backend API) — each with different data visibility rules. Clients see anonymized "Option 1, Option   2" results to prevent carrier bypassing. Agents and admins see real provider names. Role enforcement happens at both the API layer (FastAPI middleware) and database layer (Supabase Row-Level Security policies).

  ---
  How It Was Built

  Backend — FastAPI on HuggingFace Spaces

  The API is built with FastAPI (Python), chosen for its async support, automatic OpenAPI docs, and type-safe request/response modeling. It runs in a Docker container on HuggingFace Spaces on port 7860 — a cost-effective cloud hosting
  solution for the API layer.

  All database access goes through the Supabase Python SDK using a service-role key, giving the backend full unrestricted access while the frontend clients use anon keys governed by RLS policies. Authentication tokens are issued by
  Supabase Auth and validated with PyJWT on every protected route.

  File parsing uses openpyxl and pandas for Excel handling, pdfplumber for PDF support, and Pillow for the rate sheet PNG export feature. The parser pipeline is modular — each file type has its own parser function, and a central
  dispatcher routes files to the right one after detection.

  Database — Supabase (PostgreSQL)

  The schema was designed to support the full lifecycle of a rate file: upload metadata in rate_files, flattened normalized rows in parsed_rates, country-service mappings in country_service_assignments, and saved quotes in quotes. A
  settings table holds dynamic config like markup percentage, postcode zone databases, and ticker messages.

  Indexes on parsed_rates(file_id, country, weight_kg) and country_service_assignments(country, service_id) keep quote lookups fast even with large datasets. Cascade deletes ensure that removing a rate file also removes all its parsed
  rows.

  Frontend — React + Vite + Tailwind

  Two separate React apps were built and deployed independently to Vercel:
  - Admin panel (admin.zexintl.com) — file management, assignment grid, user management, settings, quote search with full provider visibility
  - Client portal (rates.zexintl.com) — quote search, history, profile management, anonymized results

  Both share the same architecture pattern: an AuthContext managing the Supabase session, an api.js Axios instance with a JWT interceptor, and a useApi hook for loading/error state. Tailwind CSS 4 handles styling — dark theme for admin,
  cleaner light-leaning theme for client.

  Mobile — React Native + Expo

  The mobile app is built with React Native and Expo 54, using Expo Router 6 for file-based routing. The app mirrors both the admin and client web experiences, with separate tab navigators rendered based on the authenticated user's role.
  Sessions persist across app restarts via AsyncStorage. File uploads use expo-document-picker to allow admins to upload rate sheets directly from their phone. The production build is distributed as a 67 MB APK built through EAS (Expo
  Application Services).

  Rate Sheets Feature

  A later addition to the platform generates formatted rate sheet images and Excel exports directly from the database. The backend uses Pillow to render rate tables as PNG files — with the ZEX logo embedded as base64, an 8-color carrier
  palette, bold text, and legible font sizing — which can be downloaded or shared to WhatsApp directly from both web and mobile.

  ---
  Deployment Architecture

  ┌─────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Component  │          Platform           │               URL                │
  ├─────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Backend API │ HuggingFace Spaces (Docker) │ aamirshamsi-zex-rates.hf.space   │
  ├─────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Admin Web   │ Vercel                      │ admin.zexintl.com                │
  ├─────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Client Web  │ Vercel                      │ rates.zexintl.com                │
  ├─────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Mobile App  │ EAS / Direct APK            │ ZEX-Rates.apk                    │
  ├─────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Database    │ Supabase                    │ ixiswyebtqgyvjfpyqod.supabase.co │
  └─────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

  ---
  Scale of the Work

  The project spans approximately:
  - 5 separate deployable components (backend, 2 web apps, mobile, database)
  - 17+ Excel file format parsers
  - 40+ REST API endpoints
  - 8 database tables with relational constraints and RLS policies
  - 4,813 Australian postcodes mapped to carrier zones
  - 3 user roles with distinct UI flows across 4 platforms
  - A production Android APK in active use

  From first principles to production across all surfaces, this represents a substantial real-world engineering effort — not a boilerplate app, but a domain-specific system designed around the genuine complexity of international freight
  pricing.

projects.title: Physical AI & Humanoid Robotics
projects.description: Physical AI & Humanoid Robotics Textbook is an interactive educational platform developed during a hackathon to simplify learning in robotics and embodied AI. The project combines a modern textbook interface with an AI-powered RAG chatbot that answers questions using contextual textbook content. It supports personalized learning, multilingual translation, and responsive UI for students and researchers exploring Physical AI, ROS 2, humanoid robotics, and Vision-Language-Action systems. The platform integrates semantic search with vector databases, enabling intelligent content retrieval and conversational learning experiences. Built with scalable modern technologies, the project demonstrates how AI can transform robotics education into a more accessible, engaging, and interactive digital experience.
projects.longDescription:
Physical AI & Humanoid Robotics Textbook is a hackathon-based educational platform designed to bridge the gap between robotics education and modern AI-driven learning systems. The project provides a structured digital textbook experience focused on Physical AI, humanoid robotics, ROS 2, robotics simulations, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, while integrating an intelligent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot for real-time question answering and interactive learning.

The platform uses semantic embeddings and vector databases to retrieve relevant textbook content dynamically, allowing users to ask natural language questions and receive context-aware AI-generated explanations. It also supports personalized learning preferences, multilingual translation capabilities, and responsive interfaces for both desktop and mobile users.

The frontend is built using a modern React/Docusaurus architecture for clean documentation and educational content presentation, while the backend uses FastAPI to manage authentication, APIs, user preferences, and AI integrations. Qdrant vector database enables semantic search, while OpenAI embedding models power intelligent retrieval and chatbot responses. The system is containerized using Docker and designed for scalable deployment with CI/CD support.

This project demonstrates the practical integration of AI, robotics education, and modern web technologies to create an engaging and intelligent self-learning ecosystem for students, researchers, and developers interested in embodied AI and humanoid robotics.

projects.title: Personal portfolio
projects.description: Full-stack personal portfolio with a built-in CMS admin panel, multi-format CV generator, and real-time GitHub sync — all self-contained with no external CMS required.
projects.longDescription:
A production-ready personal portfolio built with Next.js 16 and Tailwind CSS 4, featuring a complete content management system accessible via a password-protected admin panel. All portfolio data — projects, experience,
  tech stack, services, testimonials, and certifications — is stored in a flat-file JSON CMS and editable live without touching code.

  Key features include:
  - Admin CMS with sections for every portfolio category, protected by a hashed session cookie with edge-runtime proxy authentication
  - Multi-format CV generator producing region-specific PDF resumes (Gulf, Saudi, Emirati, Europass, USA, Canadian) using jsPDF with live data population
  - Email CV sharing — sends the generated PDF as an email attachment via Gmail SMTP
  - Project media — captures live screenshots from demo URLs via thum.io, or accepts manual image/video uploads
  - GitHub auto-sync — every admin save commits the JSON data file to GitHub via the API, keeping Vercel's ephemeral filesystem in sync
  - Light/Dark mode toggle with full theme support across all components
  - Responsive design with smooth Framer Motion animations throughout
